title: Systolic blood pressure

review.note: Drafted from the sources below; not yet reviewed by a medical professional.

measures: Blood pressure is the force of your blood pushing against the walls of your arteries. Systolic pressure is the higher number, measured when the heart beats and pumps blood. It is the first or top number in a reading such as 120/80.
context: A single reading is not enough on its own; a provider usually takes two or more readings at separate visits before deciding what it means. Normal readings also change with age, sex, and overall health.
aboveRange: Higher readings may be associated with high blood pressure
It may be primary (building up over time as you get older) or linked to another condition or a medicine you take
belowRange: Lower readings are normal for some people who feel well
In others, lower readings may be linked to a condition or a medicine, and may sometimes cause dizziness or fainting
nextStep: Discuss this result with your doctor.
